title: Marco Polo on the Silk Road
description: 1271-1275. Escort the young Marco Polo, his father Niccolo, and their trade caravan across the deserts and mountain passes of Central Asia to the court of Kublai Khan. Bandit raiders and harsh terrain threaten the route; the caravan's pack animals must survive. Victory requires bringing Marco alive to the Khan's summer palace at Shangdu.

anachronisms_found: EL_CID (Rodrigo Diaz, died 1099, Castile) placed as a caravan figure - wrong century and wrong region by nearly two hundred years; he is used to stand in for a 13th-century Venetian merchant
WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR (died 1087, Normandy/England) placed in the Polo caravan - an 11th-century Norman king has no business on the 1271 Silk Road
GENGHIS_KHAN placed as a GAIA object at the destination: Genghis died in 1227 and the Polos were received by his grandson Kublai Khan, whose hero unit exists in the editor and should have been used
KNIGHT x3 as caravan escort - heavy Latin-Christian shock cavalry crossing Persia and the Pamirs is implausible; camel riders or light cavalry escorts were available in the engine
SHEEP x6 standing in for the caravan's pack animals when TRADE_CART and camel units were available and far more representative of a Silk Road caravan
CASTLE/KEEP used to represent Shangdu, giving the Khan's summer palace generic European stone-fortress architecture; a Wonder or pagoda-style structure would have read better

issues_found: Marco Polo is represented by the WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR hero - a Norman duke of the 11th century, an entirely unrelated culture and era; a renamed generic unit (or even a Trade Cart escort figure) was available and would have been correct.
Niccolo Polo is represented by EL_CID, an 11th-century Castilian warlord - again wrong culture and wrong century for a 13th-century Venetian merchant.

GENGHIS_KHAN is placed (under GAIA) at the destination, apparently standing in for Kublai Khan. Genghis died in 1227, decades before the journey and before Shangdu was built; the text explicitly names Kublai, so the placed hero contradicts the narration.

Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so the castle, keep and archery range architecture is unspecified and could render as any culture from Britons to Aztecs - avoidable, since Mongols/Persians/Chinese/Turks were all selectable.

The caravan's 'pack animals' are SHEEP, when the engine ships Trade Carts (and camels) that would read far better as a Silk Road merchant caravan; the escort of KNIGHTS and CROSSBOWMEN is a European field force rather than hired caravan guards.
GAIA-owned CASTLE and KEEPs with PALISADE_WALL fragments are an odd, unexplained fortification set for either a Persian oasis or Shangdu's summer palace.

Marco Polo is represented by the WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR hero — an 11th-century Norman duke, wrong culture and wrong century for a 13th-century Venetian merchant. A renamed generic unit (villager, trade cart driver, even a merchant-style unit) was available and would have been correct.
Niccolo Polo is represented by EL_CID, an 11th-century Castilian warlord — again an unrelated culture and era for a Venetian trader.

GENGHIS_KHAN is placed (as GAIA) while the narration and victory text name Kublai Khan; Genghis died in 1227, 44 years before the journey depicted. Right culture, wrong person, and an avoidable anachronism given the text explicitly names Kublai.

Both active players are assigned civilization RANDOM, so the Polos' escort and the steppe bandits may render with any architecture set — Mongols/Persians/Saracens/Chinese were all available and appropriate.

The Venetian escort is composed of KNIGHT x3 and CROSSBOWMAN x2 under Latin-European heroes — a mounted knightly retinue is not what a merchant caravan hired across Persia and the Tarim; camels, trade carts, or light cavalry/skirmishers would have been closer.
TREE_PALM_FOREST x20 is used across the whole route; palms suit a Persian oasis but not the Pamir passes or the Taklamakan margins.
Pack animals are SHEEP; the engine offers Trade Carts and Camels, which would have represented a goods-bearing Silk Road caravan far better than a flock.
GAIA CASTLE + KEEP x2 for Shangdu gives the Khan's summer palace European fortification rather than any of the East Asian building sets available.
